skill.name: wizard
skill.description: Generate an interactive Bash wizard for manual setup, migrations, and state changes that need guided steps and captured values.
skill.summary: Create guided Bash scripts for repeatable manual setup and migration workflows.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally creates Bash scripts that read and write .env values, collect secrets, open URLs, and use gh to set GitHub Actions secrets. Many Markdown backtick and shell expansion alerts are false positives, but the secret-handling behavior is real. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmations before writing .env values or setting GitHub secrets, and redact secret values from all output.
Default to reading .env.example and workflow references, and ask before reading real .env files that may contain secrets.

remediation.issue: Generated browser and CLI side effects
remediation.suggestion: Require generated wizards to list target domains, file writes, and gh operations before any stage runs.

remediation.issue: Temporary file handling for environment updates
remediation.suggestion: Use a restrictive umask and cleanup trap around temporary files that may contain secret values.

semantic_findings.title: Model Instruction to Inspect Real Environment Files
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to read the repository first, including .env and .env.* files. That can expose local credentials to the model context before the user has explicitly approved reading secret-bearing files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly names .env and .env.* as setup files to inspect. Those files commonly contain credentials, so the privacy risk is direct.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Wizard Can Mutate GitHub Repository Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The template includes helpers that use the authenticated gh CLI to set repository secrets and variables. A generated wizard could change CI configuration state if the user runs it without reviewing the staged operations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper functions call gh secret set and gh variable set when gh is authenticated. The behavior is intentional, but it is a real repository side effect.

content.value_statement: Manual setup steps are easy to miss, especially when they involve external dashboards and secrets. This skill creates a guided Bash wizard for repeatable human workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides the assistant to scope a manual setup or migration before scripting.
Uses template.sh to create staged Bash wizards with progress and confirmations.
Opens browser URLs for human-driven setup steps.
Captures visible and hidden inputs from the user.
Writes idempotent .env values and can set GitHub Actions secrets or variables.
Encourages bash syntax checks, optional shellcheck, and static tracing before handoff.
limitations: Generated scripts require human input and are not fully autonomous.
The workflow can handle secrets, so every generated script needs review before running.
Third-party dashboard paths may change and should be verified against current docs.
The template assumes Bash and common local terminal tools.

use_cases.title: Onboard Developers to a Local Project
use_cases.description: Create a one-run setup wizard that collects required local values and writes them to the expected environment file.

use_cases.title: Configure Third-Party Services
use_cases.description: Guide a developer through dashboards such as payment, auth, or hosting providers and capture the values the app needs.

use_cases.title: Run a Controlled Migration
use_cases.description: Turn a manual migration checklist into ordered stages with confirmations before irreversible actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Setup Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wizard for this project setup. Read the safe setup docs first, list each stage, and ask before reading any real .env file.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Service Integration Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash wizard for adding a third-party service. Include browser steps, captured values, .env writes, and review checkpoints before secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Migration Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wizard for a one-time migration from the current state to the target state. Include irreversible-action confirmations and a final handoff summary.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Secret Setup Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wizard that maps required GitHub Actions secrets and variables, explains each gh operation, and asks for confirmation before any repository change.

output_examples.input: Create a setup wizard for Stripe test keys.
output: A staged Bash wizard that opens the Stripe dashboard.
Prompts for publishable and secret keys with the correct visibility.
Writes local environment values and sets the CI secret after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Create a migration wizard for moving from one provider to another.
output: An ordered checklist converted into interactive stages.
Confirmation gates before irreversible provider changes.
A final summary of completed and skipped actions.

output_examples.input: Create an onboarding wizard for new contributors.
output: A guided setup script for required local values.
Clear browser instructions for external accounts.
A handoff note that explains how to run and review the script.

best_practices: Review the generated script before running it, especially every write_env, set_secret, and set_var call.
Use .env.example and workflow references for planning before reading real .env files.
Keep each stage focused on one human task and confirm before side effects.
anti_patterns: Do not run a generated wizard end to end without reviewing its stages and destinations.
Do not commit one-off scripts that contain project-specific secrets or temporary setup assumptions.
Do not invent third-party dashboard steps when current documentation is unknown.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates interactive Bash wizards that guide a human through setup, migration, or configuration steps.

faq.question: Does it run the setup automatically?
faq.answer: No. The generated script asks the user to perform browser steps and confirm progress.

faq.question: Can it handle secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prompt for hidden values, write .env entries, and set GitHub Actions secrets.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with real .env files?
faq.answer: Use caution. Ask before reading real .env files and review every generated write before running the script.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should generated wizards be committed?
faq.answer: Commit them only when the setup path should be repeatable and contains no sensitive local values.
